paper.title: Serpent: A Proposal for the Advanced Encryption Standard

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Serpent-1 (32 rounds, 8 S-boxes used in bitslice mode, linear transformation, 132-word prekey recurrence with the golden-ratio constant, key padding, round keys through the S-boxes in the order S3, S2, S1, S0, S7, ...) written from the paper's description reproduces the authors' encryption vectors, sets 1-4: 514 (128-bit keys) + 578 (192-bit) + 642 (256-bit) = 1,734 ciphertexts
Decryption (inverse S-boxes from the paper, inverse linear transformation obtained by undoing each step) reproduces the authors' decryption vectors, sets 5-8: 1,734 plaintexts
The 'iterated 100 times' and 'iterated 1000 times' values of set 4 (2 vectors per key size, 12 values in all)
The inverse S-boxes printed in the paper invert the printed S-boxes (128 entries)

expected_values_source.what: the S-boxes and inverse S-boxes from appendix A.5 of the paper, and the authors' test vectors in the NESSIE printout format on Eli Biham's Serpent page ('NESSIE's test vectors for Serpent' with 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys, which the files label 'verified')
expected_values_source.note: S-boxes extracted from the PDF text and vectors copied as data by script; the program was written from the paper. Bytes of keys and blocks are used in the printed order as little-endian 32-bit words, which a single-vector trial confirmed (reversed order gives different output). The iterated tests were run on Tier-3 as well

negative_control: built with -DSERPENT_R13=12 (first rotation of the linear transformation changed from 13 to 12), 0 of 1,734 encryption vectors match, decryption and iterated checks fail and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security analysis (differential/linear bounds), its speed figures, and the earlier Serpent-0 variant with the DES S-boxes
the paper's non-bitslice description (initial and final permutations IP/FP and the tabulated linear transformation): only the equivalent bitslice form is implemented
key lengths other than 128, 192 and 256 bits, and modes of operation
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 3,468 ciphertexts or plaintexts and 12 iterated values the Serpent authors published, using the paper's S-boxes. It does not show the security claims hold.
